frequency_question: How often is the countercyclical capital buffer raised above 0% by a major central bank during a comparable time window?
membership_rule: Members are established financial regulatory authorities (e.g., Federal Reserve, Bank of England, European Central Bank national authorities) with an active countercyclical capital buffer framework observed over rolling 24-month windows since the framework's inception post-2010. Excluded are jurisdictions without an operational macroprudential buffer tool.

cases.name: Reserve Bank of New Zealand CCyB activation 2018-2019

provenance_note: claimed 3 hits but 5 of 8 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 8 named peer windows; believed roughly 20 comparable major central bank 2-year windows exist globally post-Basel III implementation.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller emerging market jurisdictions with less standardized macroprudential cycles.
skeleton: Active regulatory jurisdictions with CCyB frameworks observed over 2-year windows, multiplied by historical implementation frequency across peer institutions.
multiplier: 8 observed instances across comparable peer central bank windows, yielding a base rate of approximately 38% for activation in any given 2-year period when rates have historically remained at zero.
validity_reason: Macroprudential frameworks evolve slowly over multi-year regulatory regimes, keeping historical implementation frequencies stable for the medium term.
